text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers.
DER STANDARD

- Austria's junior coalition partner, the conservative People's Party (OeVP), has caught up with Social Democrats (SPOe) in surveys ahead of Sunday's European parliamentary elections. Some 45 percent of voters still have not decided who to vote for. About 47 precent say they would not vote for Joerg Haider's far-right Freedom Party.
- Social Minister Franz Hums wants to make people receiving emergency benefits from the state work. Austrians receive these benefits after they have been out of a job for six months.
- Petrol prices have gone up 0.10 schillings and prices for diesel und heating oil 0.20 schillings went up from Wednesday.
- Austria's largest retailer Billa, owned by German chain Rewe, will open 30 shops by the end of the year.

- Sports maker Head-Tyrolia-Mares' restructuring has cost 1.7 billion schillings. Owner Johan Eliasch, who bought the ailing firm a year ago, hopes banks will waive some million schillings worth of debts and interest.
- Austrian employer and employee representatives do not want wages to fall below the collective agreement level.
- South African paper maker Mondi will boost its stake to 50 percent from 44.4 percent in Austria's Frantschach by means of a capital injection worth 650 million schillings.
- Steel maker VA Stahl says it will save some 600 million schillings in taxes by March 31, the new balancing date.
DIE PRESSE
- Social Democrat education experts want university graduates to pay a special academic tax.
- Austria's ecologically friendly farmers will receive some 2.6 billion schillings more in EU-subsidies.
- 56 percent of Austrian firms say European Union membership has brought more advantages than disadvantages.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima wants to make Austria the centre of Central European stock markets.
KURIER
- Austrian specialists have deciphered the code in a recent letterbomb threat, which confirms extremist links to the murder of four Austrian gypsies last year.
- Cement maker Paerlmooser's pre-tax profits fell to 69 million schillings in the first half of 1996 compared to 99 million in the previous year.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Austrian haulage contractors are planning to take legal action against Austrian railways OeBB for using subsidies to lower haulage prices.
- An Austrian business visit to Beijing, led by Chancellor Franz Vranitzky, could result in a deal worth eight billion schillings for Austrian engineering group VA Technologie.
